taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "Low creeping alpine shrub with ascending branches, 1-3 dm. high".

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "1-3 dm. high".

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "Low creeping alpine shrub".

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: a shrub.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: leaves "evergreen and long-persistent on the branches after dying".

traits.clonal.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Prostrate or creeping shrubs with ascending branches", spreading into mats, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_form.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Leaves scale-like, closely imbricate".

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: leaves "decussately opposite in pairs (4-ranked)".

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: leaves "decussately opposite in pairs (4-ranked)".

traits.leaf_posture.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: leaves "closely imbricate", pressed against the stem, so each shoot looks like a four-angled cord.

traits.leaf_shape.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: scale leaves ovate to lance-ovate, as in the photos; Abrams gives only their apex and keel.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: leaves "obtuse at the apex, rounded or slightly keeled on the back".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "Leaves 3-6 mm. long".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: scale leaves 1.5 mm to 2 mm wide, as in the photos.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Flowers solitary in the axils of the leaves toward the ends of the branches".

traits.flowering_position.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: flowers "in the axils of the leaves toward the ends of the branches".

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "pedicels 6-20 mm. long, minutely puberulent".

traits.flower_posture.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: flowers "on slender elongated pedicels, nodding in anthesis".

traits.corolla_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Corolla campanulate, 4-5-lobed, the lobes much shorter than the tube".

traits.flower_merosity.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Calyx 4-5-lobed"; "Corolla campanulate, 4-5-lobed"; five in most of the photos.

traits.stamens.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Stamens 8 or 10, included".

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: bells 6 mm to 8 mm long, as in the photos; Abrams gives 4-6 mm for C. tetragona (1951 p. 305) and none for this species.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "calyx-lobes 2-3.5 mm. long, ovate, obtuse".

traits.flower_colour.note: Corolla white; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 88217384, 29622385, 127852701, 227023300, 379229319, 131530025, 128442498, 240857348): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.calyx_colour.note: Calyx lobes and pedicels red; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 88217384, 29622385, 127852701, 227023300, 379229319, 131530025, 128442498, 240857348): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Capsule globose to ovoid, 4-5-lobed and loculicidally 4-5-valved" (pp. 303-305).

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 305, Cassiope mertensiana: "capsule subglobose or ovoid, 2.5-3.5 mm. long".

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe in August and September, after the July and August flowers.

generator.params.note: Evergreen huckleberry's (vaccinium-ovatum) values, changed by hand for white mountain-heather: a low mat of many ascending branches (Abrams 1951 p. 305: "Low creeping alpine shrub with ascending branches, 1-3 dm. high"), very short internodes, sprigs of tiny scale leaves pressed to the stem and kept for years, and a few nodding bells near each shoot's tip (genus, p. 303). Not fitted to measurements.

appearance.organs.bloom.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Cassiope: "Flowers solitary in the axils", "nodding in anthesis", "Corolla campanulate"; white bells with red calyx lobes in the photos the traits cite. Drawn without a cluster, as single nodding bells about twice the capsule's size.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low heath of upright, cord-like shoots clothed in tiny, pressed, four-ranked scale leaves, hung with small white bells on red stalks. Organ cards from evergreen huckleberry's (vaccinium-ovatum), recoloured and resized by hand.

allometry.note: 0.18 m tall at 10 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
